title: Interactive Imitation Learning in Robotics: A Survey
reasoning: The paper is a survey of Interactive Imitation Learning in Robotics. It focuses on algorithms, feedback modalities, models, interfaces, and evaluation metrics for robot performance and human factors (e.g., trust, workload, safety) in human-robot interaction. It does not evaluate or benchmark religion, morals, or ethics as a primary component. Discussions of 'safety' and 'human factors' are related to practical concerns in robotics rather than explicit ethical frameworks.
